title: A Swarm of 3.5 Trillion Locusts Once Covered the West

scenes.text: The biggest swarm ever had trillions of locusts.
In 1875, Rocky Mountain locusts swarmed across the American West.
It covered about 198,000 square miles. That's bigger than California.
Estimates say 3.5 trillion insects, maybe even more.
They stripped crops in their path.
Then the species vanished by 1902. Trillions, then none.

description:
In 1875 a swarm of Rocky Mountain locusts covered about 198,000 square miles of the American West.
Estimates for the number of insects range from 3.5 trillion to 12.5 trillion.
How can a species like that disappear?
first_comment: How do you think a species with trillions just vanished?
